Subject: MAP: tokens-per-dollar reconciliation & deployment assumptions

Jamie / Acme procurement — thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, attaching the working MAP and a small sample of the pilot traffic so your engineering and procurement teams can validate assumptions. High-level asks from our side: 

- Can you confirm expected average prompt length and average generated tokens per request for the pilot (we used the sample file for our estimate but want your sign-off)?
- Do you expect steady-state concurrency that would justify continuous batching, or will traffic be highly spiky? (helps determine batching profile)
- Any requirements around KV cache persistence across requests or session affinity?

Key assumptions baked into the MAP-draft-v2.xlsx: tokens/$ a) baseline gen = 40 tokens per second at p99 latency target, b) caching reduces 1st-token cost for repeated prefixes by ~37%, c) batching improves throughput but increases tail latency for sub-50ms SLOs. See the "Cost Assumptions" tab.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Your team confirms sample traffic metrics by Tue 8/3 EOD.
2) Redwood runs a 48-hour pilot with MAP gating thresholds (traffic window and acceptance criteria) 8/10–8/12.
3) Post-pilot econ review and mutual sign-off 8/14.

Attachments: MAP-draft-v2.xlsx (working), pilot-traffic-sample.jsonl (anonymized).

Thanks — I’ll sync Ben on licensing terms and Monica on the SOC/security questionnaire routing.

— Hannah

Hannah — thanks, appreciate the clear summary and the file. Quick answers from our side after a brief check: 

- Average prompt length: 85 chars (roughly 18 tokens). Average model generation: 120 tokens per response (on our current dataset) but we see a long tail (some responses up to ~800 tokens for full patient summaries). For the pilot we can scope to the shorter summaries (median ~90 tokens).
- Traffic shape: initial pilot traffic will be steady (40–60 reqs/min) during business hours, but production will be spiky around batch import windows. Concurrency for pilot: peak ~25 concurrent requests.
- Cache: we do have repeated prefixes for templated summaries — persisting KV between requests for the same session is desirable but not required for the MVP.

We attached a short CSV (sent separately) with percentiles that map to your sample; if you need any different slices (by patient type / summary length) let us know. Also — one procurement question: can you commit to a max-burst cap for Dedicated during pilot (so our infra team can size VPC egress)?

— Jamie
Jamie Ortiz
Head of Integrations (Acme Health)

Subject: Re: MAP: tokens-per-dollar reconciliation & deployment assumptions

Jamie / team — quick tech notes to align expectations for the pilot and the MAP econ cells: 

- Batching: for the pilot concurrency you described (peak ~25), continuous batching yields modest unit-cost savings (~8–12%) but only if average latency can tolerate ~60–120ms extra tail. If you need p95 <200ms end-to-end we should run an isolated perf test with your sample to pick an optimal batch window.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching helps when you have repeated templated prefixes (your note indicates you do). In our internal tests, for similar workloads we saw a per-request token reduction of ~30–40% for repeat-heavy routes; however, cache effectiveness depends on session affinity — if requests are across many short-lived sessions the hit-rate drops quickly.
- Long-tail tokens: since you have occasional 800-token outputs, the cost per request will have a skewed distribution. For MAP economics we recommend mapping cost buckets by percentile (median, p90, p99) rather than using a single mean. That will prevent surprise overages.

Operational ask: can your engineering team provide a one-hour window to run a 1k-req synthetic run against a staging endpoint (we’ll provide a load harness)? That will give us the precise batching vs latency tradeoffs for your traffic slice.

— Karthik
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

If there are no objections I’ll lock the MAP milestone dates in the shared doc and send an updated mutual action plan with sign-off checkboxes. Goal: pilot complete and econ sign-off by 8/14 so procurement and finance can finalize contract terms by end of month.
